title: Building a Game for the first time in my Life!
author: anomitro_munshi
selftext:
Hi everyone! This is my first attempt at making a game. I’ve always loved playing games, so I decided to try building one using Godot, with help from Claude Code.

I have plenty of game ideas… but not enough tokens 😥😂

I’d also love some advice: how do you create polished 3D characters with smooth animations in Godot? Is that mainly about the models and animations, or would switching to Unity help? And is Unity free for beginners?

comments.author: Cupheadvania
comments.body: looks great! how did you make the 2D animations?

replies.author: anomitro_munshi
replies.body: totally with godot 4 and gdscripts..its a fully vibe coded game..i gave the AI some ref of actual moves and images from pinterst..like muay thigh spin kick reference, AI made it for me..ofc i tested and gave feedback in a loop.

comments.author: teapot_RGB_color
comments.body:
Oh, you did not exactly choose an easy genre to start with...

I mean, if it creates a bit of fun, then go for it. But that being said.. Are you familiar with  fighting games?

replies.author: anomitro_munshi
replies.body: Ya I've played alot of fighting games.

replies.author: teapot_RGB_color
replies.body:
Yeah so for 3D characters, the advice is don't go there I guess...

It will drag you down into a sinkhole of balance issues.

Best advice I have is to set up custom animation editors, I don't know about godot, but Unity is not intuitive in fighting game animation, you need to bypass a lot of the original setup make it work for frequency sync, or.. easier way, just lock the framerate. Tweaking animation and hit boxes is a PITA. It helps a lot for me that I've been using Unity for  more than a decade and can communicate using the internal vocabulary of unity with the LLM
